sections.html:
Melrose is a small Middlesex County city about seven miles north of Boston, in the middle of the triangle formed by Interstate 93, Interstate 95 and U.S. Route 1. It borders Malden, Saugus, Stoneham and Wakefield.

The city covers only 4.77 square miles, so almost every house sits close to a pond, a park or a train stop. The 2020 census counted 29,817 residents and 12,614 housing units, with 3.7 percent of those units vacant. Melrose peaked at 33,180 people in 1970, slipped for four decades, then grew 10.5 percent between 2010 and 2020. Median age is 40.7, and the city runs on a mayor and an eleven-member council.

Melrose began as North Malden, a lightly settled farming area that became its own town in 1850 and took its name from Melrose, Scotland. The Boston and Maine Railroad had added three stops by 1845, and Boston workers who wanted a country setting started commuting from here. The town annexed the highlands from Stoneham in 1853, which set today's borders, and it became a city at the turn of 1900.

The first lots were carved out of farmland in the second half of the 1800s, so plenty of Melrose houses are old, and old houses bring their own checklists at sale time. Those three railroad stops are still the commuter rail stations on the Haverhill Line.

There are eight named neighborhoods, and buyers and sellers tend to place a house by one of them.

  • Cedar Park and Wyoming, which share names with commuter rail stops
  • Melrose Highlands, the part annexed from Stoneham
  • Downtown Melrose, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1982
  • Horace Mann, East Side and Mount Hood on the eastern side of the city
  • Oak Grove and Pine Banks, near the Malden line and Pine Banks Park

Ell Pond sits near the center of the city. Swains Pond and Towners Pond are on the east side near Mount Hood Golf Club, and the eastern reaches of the Middlesex Fells Reservation fall inside the city line. A house near water or park land can show different grading, drainage and basement conditions than one on a hilltop, so a buyer's inspector will study the lower floors.

Melrose has no major highway of its own, only a short stretch of Route 99. Residents reach Route 1 in Saugus, Interstate 93 in Stoneham, Route 16 in Everett and Route 128 or Interstate 95 in Wakefield.

Three Haverhill Line commuter rail stations serve the city: Melrose Highlands, Melrose/Cedar Park and Wyoming Hill. MBTA bus routes 131, 132 and 137 also run through, and the Orange Line terminal at Oak Grove sits just across the line in Malden. Rail access to Boston is a big part of why Melrose has long been a commuter suburb.

sections.h2: Tax rates and remaining due dates
sections.html:
Melrose bills real estate tax quarterly across a July 1 to June 30 fiscal year, with estimated bills first and bills built on assessed values last. Homes carry the fiscal 2026 residential rate of $11.47 per $1,000, while commercial, industrial and personal property is taxed at $20.61. Two installments are still ahead in the FY2027 schedule.

QuarterDue date
3rd quarterFebruary 1, 2027
4th quarterMay 3, 2027

The August and November bills come around again every year.

Values are set as of January 1 each year. Visit the assessor on City Hall's first floor, 562 Main Street, or phone 781-979-4104. Hours run Monday through Thursday from 8:30 am to 4 pm, and Friday from 8:30 am to 12:30 pm. Field inspections are underway across the city as part of keeping assessments current, so do not be surprised by a visit.

The treasurer and collector offers an online request for a municipal lien certificate, which shows what taxes you owe. Taxes owed to the city appear on that certificate and are settled at closing. Current details are on the Melrose assessor page and the real estate tax page.

A Melrose seller needs a fire department smoke and carbon monoxide certificate, a title search, and usually a real estate attorney.

  • Smoke and CO certificate: phone once the closing date is set, since the rules turn on the house's construction year and its last building permit date.
  • Alarm age: a battery smoke alarm that is over 10 years old, or undated, gets replaced with a sealed 10-year photoelectric unit that has a hush feature.
  • Municipal lien certificate: request it online through the treasurer and collector.
  • Attorney and title: expect to hire a real estate attorney; they are standard in Massachusetts sales.
  • Deed tax: the deeds excise in Chapter 64D, Section 1 is set per $500 of sale price. The registry or your attorney can give today's figure.

The state also bars sellers from conditioning an offer on a buyer's waiver of a home inspection for certain residential sales, under 760 CMR 74. Ask your attorney if your sale is covered.

Collect your latest tax bill, any water balance, a mortgage payoff statement and receipts for roof, electrical or foundation work. If tenants live in the house, add copies of the leases. For an inherited house, bring the papers that show who may sign the deed. A buyer who sees a complete folder can quote a firm price and a closing date you can rely on.

The age of the house drives most of the trouble: repair lists, alarm upgrades and inspection findings. Older homes can need electrical, roof or foundation work that a buyer financing with a mortgage may ask to have fixed before closing.

Others are selling an inherited house, handling an estate, or managing a rental with tenants still in place. Each of those adds paperwork, and the timeline can stretch while the fire certificate, lien certificate and title work come together. Cash Home Buyers works with owners in these spots and can view a Melrose property as it stands.

Dropping mortgage approval removes the step where many conventional deals stall. Describe the house, let us review it, and if you proceed the usual Massachusetts requirements remain.

  • The fire department's compliance certificate is still required.
  • The deed is still recorded at the registry of deeds.
  • Taxes owed to the city show up on the municipal lien certificate and are settled at closing.
  • An attorney still does the title work.

What you skip is the buyer's loan schedule, appraisal and financing contingency. Set the offer beside what a listing would net once repairs, showings and waiting are counted.

faqs.q: Is Melrose a town or a city?
faqs.a: Melrose is a city. It became the Town of Melrose in 1850 and was incorporated as a city at the turn of 1900, with a mayor and an eleven-member city council.

faqs.q: What is the Melrose residential tax rate?
faqs.a: For FY2026, homes are taxed at $11.47 per $1,000 of assessed value, and commercial, industrial and personal property at $20.61.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell a house in Melrose?
faqs.a: Yes. The fire department must certify that your alarms meet the sale requirements, and it charges a fee. Call Melrose's department to schedule.

faqs.q: Which commuter rail stations serve Melrose?
faqs.a: Three Haverhill Line stations serve Melrose: Melrose Highlands, Melrose/Cedar Park and Wyoming Hill. The Orange Line stop at Oak Grove is in neighboring Malden.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Melrose assessment?
faqs.a: The Melrose Assessment Department answers at 781-979-4104. It sits on City Hall's first floor, 562 Main Street, with hours Monday through Thursday 8:30 am to 4 pm and Friday 8:30 am to 12:30 pm.
